nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a finite simplicial $(d-1)$-sphere, that is, a finite geometric simplicial complex in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose underlying space is homeomorphic to the unit sphere of $\mathbb{R}^d$. Then for every natural number $j \le d$, the h-vector of $X$ satisfies $h_j = h_{d-j}$. Here $h_j = \sum_{i=0}^{j} (-1)^{j-i} \binom{d-i}{j-i} f_{i-1}$, where $f_{-1} = 1$ and $f_k$ is the number of $k$-dimensional faces of $X$.
nodes.title: Dehn–Sommerville equations

nodes.summary: For a finite simplicial $(d-1)$-sphere $X$ and a natural number $i$, the $i$-th extended face number of $X$ is $1$ if $i = 0$, and is the number $f_{i-1}(X)$ of $(i-1)$-dimensional faces of $X$ if $i \ge 1$. Thus it equals $f_{i-1}(X)$ under the convention $f_{-1}(X) = 1$.
nodes.title: Extended face numbers

nodes.summary: For a finite simplicial $(d-1)$-sphere $X$ and a natural number $k$, $f_k(X)$ is the number of $k$-dimensional faces of $X$, that is, of faces with exactly $k+1$ vertices.
nodes.title: Face numbers of a simplicial sphere

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, a finite simplicial $(d-1)$-sphere is a geometric simplicial complex $K$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^d$ with finitely many faces whose underlying space is homeomorphic to the unit sphere $S^{d-1} = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^d : \|x\| = 1\}$.
